days.title: Glaciers and Northern Heights
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Grjotbrean
stops.detail: Immediately north of the peak, below the north face, lies the large Grjotbrean glacier, which divides into two arms and reaches down to an altitude of around 1,800 meters above sea level.

stops.name: Gråsubrean
stops.detail: To the northeast, the glacier surface of the Gråsubrean directly joins the peak structure, and to the direct southeast of the peak, the Glitterbrean stretches down.

days.title: Southern Lakes and Western Valleys
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Oberer und Niederer Steinbuvatnet
stops.detail: To the south are the lakes Upper and Lower Steinbuvatnet, which are only ice-free in summer.

stops.name: Glitterholet
stops.detail: The name of Glittertind probably comes from the nearby stream Glitra, which flows through the high valley Glitterholet to the west of the mountain.

days.title: Mountain Huts and Ascent Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Glitterheim
stops.detail: The mountain can be climbed from two sides, with the DNT huts Spiterstulen in Visdalen and Glitterheim in Veodalen serving as bases.

stops.name: Skauthoe
stops.detail: It first leads steeply up the eastern slope of the Visdalen to a rise and then flatter around the summit of Skauthoe into the extensive undulating terrain around the prominent Skauta stream, which must be crossed without a bridge on stones lying in the stream, which can be difficult if the water level is high (snowmelt in spring, heavy rain).

stops.name: Steindalens
stops.detail: After that, the marked path leads upwards through the lower part of the Steindalen, where another stream must be crossed without a bridge.
